nodes.name: Copper electrodeposition on pretreated carbon felt
nodes.procedure: Carbon felt (Beijing Great Wall Co., Ltd) with dimensions of 1.25 cm x 0.5 cm x 0.5 cm, and a total geometric surface area of 3 cm², was used as a template. Previously, carbon felt was treated with ultrasound in ethanol for 5 min for degreasing, degassing, and improving wettability. Copper electroplating was carried out in a citrate electrolyte at a current density of 10 mAcm⁻² for 2 h with a magnetic stirrer. For anodes we used copper plates. Next, the sample was washed in hot (60°C) and room (25°C) temperature distillate and dried at 100°C for 1 h. The average weight of the coating was 36 mg. This sample was labeled Cu-CF.

nodes.name: Low-rate cobalt electrodeposition on Cu-CF
nodes.procedure: Cobalt was deposited on the prepared Cu-CF substrate by electrodeposition at current density of 5 mAcm⁻² with fixed charge of 54 C (time = 60 min). For anodes carbon rods were used. After electrodeposition, the sample was washed in hot (60°C) and room temperature (25°C) distillate and dried at 100°C for 1 h. The synthesized composites were labeled CC-5, CC-10 and CC-20.

nodes.name: Annealing CC-5 to CCO-500
nodes.procedure: The sample selected at the first step of synthesis (CC-5) was annealed at temperature of 500°C for 2h. The synthesized composite was labeled CCO-500.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show smooth morphology change; Cu-CF precursor thickness 1.2±0.2 μm increasing to 1.5 μm after Co deposition; less compact morphology for CC-5/CC-10 vs CC-20; template burnout with T>400°C forming microtubes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Morphological features of the Cu-Co composite investigated by scanning electron microscopy are shown in Fig. 2. The thickness of the copper coating in the Cu-CF precursor is 1.2 ± 0.2 μm... There is a gradual burnout of the carbon template with increasing temperature.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms low Co content up to 3 wt% across 1st step samples (CC-5: 0.5 wt%, CC-10: 1.5 wt%, CC-20: 2.9 wt%); Cu:Co ratio unchanged during annealing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the results of energy dispersion and X-ray diffraction analysis, the formation of a system with a low cobalt content (up to 3 wt%)... For samples obtained at low electrodeposition rates, the fraction of cobalt is 0.5 and 1.5 wt% for CC-5 and CC-10...

nodes.characterization_summary: 1st step samples show Cu-cubic phase (Fm-3m) with crystallite sizes 23-28 nm; CC-5 and CC-10 also show CuO-monoclinic phase; average crystallinity index 90±2%. 2nd step shows phase evolution to CuO dominant in CCO-500 with crystallite size 73 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results of the XRD analysis of the samples are shown in Fig. 4... According to the standards from the COD database (Table 2), these reflexes correspond to copper... The CCO-500 sample is the most crystalline (93.5%)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Best CCO-500 shows overpotential -40 mV (LSV) and -235 mV (galvanostatic at 10 mA/cm²); 1st step CC-5: -160 mV @10 mA/cm²; Tafel slopes 84-149 mV/dec.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The best sample, a mixed cobalt-copper oxide annealed at 500°C, showed a stable nominal overpotential of -235 mV in the galvanostatic test and -40 mV at linear sweep voltammetry.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV determines Cdl for ECSA calculation (C*=0.08 mF/cm²): CC-5 (350 cm²), CCO-300 (1063 cm²), CCO-400 (3350 cm², local max), CCO-500 (688 cm²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ECSA was estimated based on the determination of the double-layer capacitance (Cdl) from the linear dependence of the current density from the sweep rate in the region of non-Faraday processes.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows impedance of 3 Ohms for CCO-500; equivalent circuit fitting gives Rct values 0.69-2.8 Ohms and CPE parameters indicating diffusion limitations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electroactive surface area for the sample was 688 cm² at an impedance of 3 Ohms... The results of impedance measurements were processed in the EIS Spectrum Analyzer software.
